newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil maintains downtrend.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil maintains downtrend.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps continued to ignore the gains made on London's gas oil futures to sustain its downtrend on abundant supplies and slow demand, traders said Friday.
"The market is flooded," one broker said. "There is talk of two gas oil cargoes floating off Singapore and one off China which could not find a home."
Brokers said the volume involved could be as much as 400,000-600,000 tonnes.

They also said that ullage was tight in China and in Hong Kong. On Thursday, majors and a trader continued to sell physical gas oil agressively to as low as $27.70 per barrel for early February lifting, free-on-board basis Singapore.
February gas oil swaps was last quoted down at $27.20/$27.35 a barrel, against Thursday's $27.50/$27.70. March was last quoted at $27.30/$27.50, down from Thrsday's $27.45/$27.65.
The market traded in the morning at $27.35 for February.

The jet fuel/gas oil spread was bid at $1.80 for March, down from Thursday's $1.90 per barrel, while March was bid at $1.40. Fuel oil also continued to dip with January, February and March quoted at the same level of $108.00/$109.50 a tonne. January was last quoted at $109.00/$110.00 on Thursday.
Brokers said if the market were able to break the $105-per-tonne mark, it would easily plunge to $100.00 before buyers start appearing in bigger numbers.
